text_en: Financial Rules Changing From 1 Oct 2023: September is ending, and October is about to begin. Starting from the beginning of October, some changes will take place in matters related to money. These changes will directly impact the pockets of ordinary people. In October, many rules will change, including those for credit cards, debit cards, special fixed deposits and others. If you know about them in advance, you can wisely avoid the additional burden on your purse. 1. Changes in credit card and debit card rules. From October 1, 2023, a key change related to credit cards and debit cards is coming. From that month, when taking a new credit card or debit card, customers will have the freedom to choose the card network provider. That is, customers can decide in advance which provider's card they want, such as Visa, Mastercard or RuPay. Until now, banks have been issuing cards with whichever provider service they preferred, regardless of customer opinion. 2. Indian Bank extends the deadline for its special FDs. Indian Bank, one of the large public sector banks, had earlier launched special fixed deposits for its customers under the names 'Ind Super 400' and 'Ind Supreme 300 Days', and has now extended their deadline to October 31, 2023. Indian Bank is offering higher than usual interest rates on these two FD schemes. 3. IDBI Amrit Mahotsav FD scheme. IDBI Bank is running a special FD scheme for its customers under the name 'Amrit Mahotsav'. Under this scheme, customers are paid a higher interest rate than a regular FD. This is a special FD scheme of 375 and 444 days. The deadline for this FD ends on October 31, 2023. That means you have only one month left to invest in this special scheme that can earn you higher interest income. 4. Changes in TCS rules. From October 1, there will be a major change in TCS (Tax collection at source) rules. If you spend more than the prescribed limit on foreign travel in a financial year, or invest in foreign equity, mutual funds, crypto assets and so on... then TCS must be paid. If you spend more than Rs 7 lakh abroad, TCS of up to 20 percent may have to be paid. 5. SBI WeCare scheme. SBI, the largest public sector bank in the country, is running a special FD scheme for senior citizens for a period of 5 to 10 years. The deadline for this scheme ends on September 30. The market expects the bank to extend this scheme. However, the bank has not yet officially announced anything about this. So, if you want to invest in this scheme, do it today. 6. LIC policy revival campaign. If your LIC policy has lapsed, you have a golden opportunity to revive it. Life Insurance Corporation of India has launched a special revival campaign between September 1 and October 31, 2023. By paying some penalty, you can restart your lapsed LIC policy. 7. Deadline for exchanging Rs 2000 notes. If you have Rs 2,000 notes, you must exchange them this month itself. The RBI has given people a deadline of September 30, 2023 only to exchange the pink notes they have at banks. There is no information on extending this deadline. Lokmat News Network. Mumbai: This year, a total of 3,20,710 seats are available from the Mumbai division for Class 11 admissions. Of these, 1,74,580 seats are in the commerce stream. 37,700 seats in the arts stream, 1,02,270 seats in the science stream and 5,660 seats in the HSVC stream are included. Compared with last year, the total available Class 11 seats have decreased by 40. This year, Class 11 commerce seats increased by 400 and arts seats by 700, while science seats decreased by 1,140. This year the Class 10 results rose due to internal assessment, so there was a possibility that the total Class 11 seats would increase for student admissions; however, total seats decreased by 40. Meanwhile, the education department has already given an assurance that no student will be deprived of admission. In the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai area, 48,410 seats are available in Mumbai South division. Mumbai North has 51,230 seats, while Mumbai West has 95,710 seats. According to information on the Class 11 website on Monday evening, 2,37,939 students have registered for Class 11, and applications of 2,19,533 students have been verified. So far, 5,592 students have taken admission through colleges' quota management. In the Mumbai division, 20,716 seats are available for in-house admissions, 87,811 seats for the minority quota, and 15,853 seats from the management quota.

Delhi: When a man's head was searched at Terminal 3 of IGI Airport, 630.45 grams of gold was found hidden in a pouch under his hair. The recovered gold is reported to be worth about 30.55 lakh. Nowadays smugglers try to carry out gold smuggling through new methods. But because of the alertness of customs officers, their plans are foiled. A similar case came to light at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport. Where a passenger arriving from Abu Dhabi had hidden about 600 grams of gold inside a hair wig, which is reported to be worth more than Rs 30 lakh in the market. In this case, the smuggler has been arrested. According to the Customs department, the search operation was ongoing at Terminal 3 of Indira Gandhi International Airport. Then, on suspicion, one passenger was singled out. Then that person was searched, and it was found that he was wearing a wig on his head. The wig looked somewhat suspicious to customs officers, because smugglers had used this same trick for smuggling many times before; but due to vigilance, they had been caught. On Wednesday, at Terminal 3 of Indira Gandhi International Airport, after searching the bag of a man returning from Abu Dhabi, customs officers were astonished when they took out the wig. At Terminal 3 of Indira Gandhi International Airport, in fact, a yellow pouch had been stuck under the wig on this man's head. When officials opened this pouch, 630.45 grams of gold was found inside. The recovered gold is reported to be worth about 30.55 lakh. #WATCH | Delhi: A gold smuggling case booked on a passenger from Abu Dhabi at IGI Airport T3; approx 630.45g of gold worth Rs 30.55 lakhs was concealed inside his wig & rectum. Accused arrested; further probe underway: Customs Commissioner Office(Source: Delhi Customs) pic.twitter.com/2faJD8f1Vu Customs department officials also made a video of the entire incident, in which officials are seen removing the wig from the man's head. The video further shows that a yellow pouch had been stuck under the wig on the man's head. Officials have arrested the man who brought gold hidden inside the wig for now and are interrogating him. It is believed that this man may be linked to a major gold smuggling gang. Note that in recent years, bizarre gold smuggling cases have come to light. But in most cases, these smugglers are caught thanks to the alertness of the customs department. Officials have several times said in these cases that such people work as couriers for a smuggling gang. In this, people are paid 15 to 20 thousand rupees as commission for smuggling gold into the country.

In the next two hundred years, due to global warming, the monsoon system that affects India the most will become much weaker. This will cause an extreme shortage of rain and water. When global warming first began to be discussed, many questions were raised about the scientific basis of such assessments. But gradually those questions fell silent. Now there is no room for disagreement on the reality that the Earth's average temperature is rising and, as a result, the climate crisis is intensifying. Scientists around the world now feel that the path of modern development on which we are walking may become the cause of our destruction. As a result, today we have neither clean air to breathe nor clean water left to drink. But now an even greater danger is coming. The picture of the future is very frightening. If everything continues like this, by 2030 ten crore people will fall into the jaws of death solely because of the heating earth. A study report commissioned by twenty developing countries has expressed this fear. Due to global warming, by 2030 the GDP of the United States and China may fall by 2.1 percent, while India's GDP may fall by up to five percent. As the earth heats up, greenhouse gas emissions are increasing. As a result, ice accumulated at the earth's poles is melting rapidly, due to which sea levels are rising. This is a dire warning bell for cities and metropolises on the coast, and for many island countries. In fact, this is a question of survival for them. Due to climate change, five million people die every year from air pollution, hunger and disease. By 2030, six million people will die every year for this reason. At this rate, over the next fifteen years, that is by 2030, nine crore people will fall victim to climate change. Ninety percent of these deaths will occur in developing countries. This danger has arisen from the indiscriminate exploitation of natural resources, deforestation and new modern development technologies. This study report by developing countries assesses the economic impact of climate change on 184 countries in 2010 and 2030. Due to climate change, world GDP is losing 1.6 percent every year, that is, twelve hundred kharab dollars. If the Earth's temperature keeps rising like this due to climate change, this loss will become 3.2 percent by 2030, and by the end of this century this figure will exceed ten percent. Whereas, building a low-carbon economy while fighting climate change will cost only half a percent of world GDP. The impact of climate change will be greatest on poor countries. By 2030, their GDP may fall by up to eleven percent. According to one estimate, a one degree Celsius rise in the earth's temperature causes a ten percent decline in agricultural production.
